# co-maintainer

> co-maintainer learns a GitHub repository from its code, pull requests, and history, then reviews pull requests and local changes against that knowledge.

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/getting-started.md

# Getting started

A tool that helps to review your changes.

## Overview

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  install[Install CLI] --> auth[gh auth login]
  auth --> probe[probe]
  probe --> init[init]
  init --> review[review]
  init --> sync["sync <br/>(to keep your context up to date)"]
```

## Install

```sh
npm install -g co-maintainer
co-maintainer --version
```

## Review my changes now

In a clone of the repository, replace `owner/repo` with your repository:

```sh
gh auth login
co-maintainer init owner/repo
co-maintainer review
```

## Ways to use it

| You want | Where it runs | Typical entry | Read |
| -------- | ------------- | ------------- | ---- |
| Try a PR or local branch quickly | Your machine | `review` or `review owner/repo 123` | [local-review](local-review.md) · [PR review](local-pr-review.md) |
| Team-wide PR reviews without everyone running the CLI | Your server + GitHub App | `set` App credentials, then `serve` | [serve](serve.md) |
| Operate repos, tokens, concurrency | Browser on the server | Dashboard after `serve` | [dashboard](dashboard.md) |
| Review a local diff without every developer running init/sync | Laptop + server | `set --remote-host` then `review --remote` | [remote-review](remote-review.md) |
| Refresh guides after main moves | Same place as `init` | `sync owner/repo` | [sync](sync.md) |
| Review pushes to `main` without PRs | Your server (`serve`), with the GitHub App or CI | Tick **Push** in the App's events, or add the CI workflow | [commit-watch-review](commit-watch-review.md) |

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/probe.md

# `probe`

Read-only research on a GitHub repository. `probe` samples pull requests and
commit history, then prints a recommended `co-maintainer init` command with
sensible `--include-*` and `--max-*` flags, plus an **estimate** of what that
command will cost in time and tokens. It does not call the AI and does not
write guide files.

## Before you run

| Check | Why |
| ----- | --- |
| [Install](getting-started.md#install) `co-maintainer` | `probe` is a CLI command |
| [GitHub auth](authentication.md) (`gh auth login` or a PAT) | `probe` only reads the repo via the API |
| [Defaults](configuration.md) with `co-maintainer set` (optional) | Skips repeating `--auth=...` on every run |
| Read access to `owner/repo` | Private repos need a token or `gh` login that can see them |

If `probe` fails, fix GitHub access first (`gh auth status`), not co-maintainer.

## Usage

```sh
co-maintainer set --auth=gh
co-maintainer probe owner/repo
co-maintainer probe              # repo from the git remote of the current directory
co-maintainer probe owner/repo --run   # probe, then run the recommended init
```

Output is a **recommended** block: a full `co-maintainer init ...` line
you can copy, followed by an **estimate** and a **next** block.

## Parameters

| Flag | Meaning |
| ------ | ----- |
| `owner/repo` | Repository to research (optional, read from the git remote when omitted) |
| `--auth=gh` | Use the GitHub CLI (default when unset: `gh`, or value from `set` / config) |
| `--auth=pat` | Use `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `--github-pat=...`, or `set --github-pat=...` |
| `--github-pat=...` | PAT for `--auth=pat` when not in env or config |
| `--env=PATH` | Load env vars from a file (see [Configuration](configuration.md)) |
| `--gh-concurrent=N` | Parallel GitHub requests while sampling PR details (default `1`, minimum `1`) |
| `--run` | After printing the plan, run the recommended `init` in the same process |
| `--json` | One JSON document on stdout, no prompts. Cannot be used with `--run` |
| `--debug` | Verbose logs on stderr |
| `--log-time` | Print timing for each probe phase |

`probe` ignores `--include-*`, `--max-*`, and AI flags. Those appear on the
**recommended `init` command** in the output when the analysis suggests them.

## The estimate

The `estimate` block says how many AI jobs the recommended `init` would queue
(`extract` and `synth`), a token range, a time range, and a dollar range. It
is a **planning estimate, not a bill**:

- Job counts come from the same inputs the real run uses, so the shape is
  exact.
- Dollars need a price for both `--low-model` and `--high-model`. They come
  from OpenRouter's public `/api/v1/models`, cached for 24 hours. With no
  price there is no dollar line rather than a guessed one.
- Time and per-job tokens come from this repository's own recorded jobs when
  four or more exist, and from the cm-dx-lab calibration otherwise. The line
  says which one it used.

`--run` runs the recommended `init` in the same process after printing the
plan, which is the "look then do" step in one command. It is the same code
path the dashboard uses, not a re-spawn.

## JSON output

With `--json`, stdout is a single JSON object (`schemaVersion` `1`) and the
progress lines go to stderr. Fields: `command` (`probe`), `repo`,
`recommended` (the `init` line), `research` (pull request and commit counts,
the `maxPrMonths`, `maxCommits` and `maxPullRequestChangeLines` windows, with
`null` for no limit, and `reasons[]`), `estimate` (`extract`, `synth`, and
`[low, high]` ranges for `tokensIn`, `tokensOut`, `seconds` and `usd`, plus the
`cost` line and its `basis`), and `durationMs`. `usd` is `null` when no price
is known. Errors with `--json` are JSON on stdout as well.

`--run` with `--json` exits with code 2, because the probe and the `init`
would be two documents on one stdout. Run `probe --json`, then the
`recommended` line with `--json`.

## What it looks at

- Repository metadata and latest release (if any)
- Pull request list (updated time, sampling across years)
- A bounded sample of PR diffs for size and activity
- Default-branch commit history

Use the printed `init` line as-is for a first run, or tighten limits if the repo
is huge and you want a cheaper `init`. Next step: [`init`](init.md).

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/init.md

# `init`

First-time knowledge build for a GitHub repository. `init` fetches sources from
GitHub, runs AI synthesis, and writes review guides under your co-maintainer
config directory (not inside the git clone). Expect minutes of runtime and
non-trivial API cost on large repos.

## Before you run

| Check | Why |
| ----- | --- |
| [Install](getting-started.md#install) `co-maintainer` | `init` is a CLI command |
| [`probe`](probe.md) on the same `owner/repo` (recommended) | Gives a ready-made `init` line with limits and `--include-*` flags |
| [GitHub auth](authentication.md) | Reads the repo through `gh` or a PAT |
| [AI provider](providers.md) | A key and both models via `co-maintainer set` or flags. There is no default model |

Run [`probe`](probe.md) first when you are unsure which `--max-*` limits to use.

## Usage

```sh
co-maintainer set --auth=gh --ai=openrouter --token=YOUR_KEY \
  --low-model=openai/gpt-oss-120b --high-model=openai/gpt-5.6-luna

co-maintainer probe owner/repo
# copy the recommended init line from probe output, for example:
co-maintainer init owner/repo --include-codebase --include-pull-requests \
  --max-pr-months=12 --max-commits=500
```

If AI settings are missing, the CLI prompts for provider, API key, and models.
Values from `set`, `--env=PATH`, or flags are not asked again.

## Parameters

| Flag | Meaning |
| ------ | ----- |
| `owner/repo` | Repository to analyze (required) |
| `--auth=gh` | GitHub CLI (default, or from `set` / config) |
| `--auth=pat` | Personal access token (see [Authentication](authentication.md)) |
| `--github-pat=...` | PAT when not in env or config |
| `--env=PATH` | Load env vars from a file |
| `--ai=openrouter` | AI provider (`openrouter`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `opencode-zen` or `opencode-go`). Required, see [AI providers](providers.md) |
| `--token=...` | Provider API key |
| `--low-model=...` | Model for extraction steps |
| `--high-model=...` | Model for synthesis steps |
| `--include-codebase` | Include default-branch tree and files |
| `--include-pull-requests` | Include PR metadata and discussions |
| `--include-pull-request-changes` | Include PR diffs |
| `--include-commit-history` | Include commit messages on the default branch |
| `--include-how-repo-works` | Include issues / workflow signals when available |
| `--agent-instructions=REGEX` | Files to read as agent instruction files for `INSTRUCTIONS.md`. Default `(^\|/)AGENTS\.md$`. A blank value turns it off, see [Agent instruction files](#agent-instruction-files) |
| `--agent-instructions-max-chars=N` | Cap on `INSTRUCTIONS.md` in characters. Default `6000`, `0` or below for no limit |
| `--max-pr-months=N` | Limit how far back PR history goes |
| `--max-commits=N` | Limit commits scanned on the default branch |
| `--max-pull-request-change-lines=N` | Skip oversized PR diffs |
| `--max-comment=N` | Cap discussion comments kept per pull request |
| `--only-request-changed-pr` | Keep only pull requests with at least one `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review |
| `--pr-state=open,closed,merged` | Keep a comma-separated subset of `open`, `closed`, and `merged` |
| `--gh-concurrent=N` | Parallel GitHub fetches (default `1`) |
| `--ai-concurrent=N` | Parallel AI jobs (default `3`) |
| `--json` | One JSON document on stdout, no prompts (see [JSON output](#json-output)) |
| `--debug` | Verbose logs on stderr |
| `--log-time` | Print timing per phase |

**Include flags:** If you pass **any** `--include-*` on the command line, only
the flags you list are enabled. With no `--include-*` flags, all sources default
to on (unless a prior `init` stored different choices in config for this repo).

**Pull request filters:** `--only-request-changed-pr` applies inside the
`--max-pr-months` window. A dismissed review does not count. Dropped pull
requests skip comment and diff downloads. The run logs
`only request-changed pr · kept N · dropped N`. Off by default.
`--pr-state` takes `open`, `closed`, and `merged`, separated by commas.
`closed` means closed and not merged. Omit it to keep every state. The listing
cache is stored per state set, so a different set is not filled from the
previous listing.

Both are saved for the repo. A later [`sync`](sync.md) without the flag
keeps the saved choice. `--only-request-changed-pr` does not turn itself off.
To collect every state again, pass `--pr-state=open,closed,merged`.

Limits and include defaults can also come from [per-repo config](configuration.md#per-repo-memory) after the first successful run.

## What it writes

Under `<config dir>/repos/owner/repo/` (see [Caching](caching.md)):

- `SKILL.md` and `CODEBASE.md`
- `PR_REVIEW_GUIDE.md` and related review guides when PR sources were included
- `INSTRUCTIONS.md` and `RULES.json`, only when an agent instruction file matches
  (see [Agent instruction files](#agent-instruction-files))

Every file is written by the AI provider. There is no offline or AI-free build,
so `init` and [`sync`](sync.md) refuse to run when no provider is configured.

`SKILL.md` holds the contribution guidance and links to `CODEBASE.md` for the
codebase sections (layout, style, tests, development and debugging), so the same
text is not repeated in both files and paid for twice in a review prompt.
`CODEBASE.md` is where that text actually lives.

Findings read out of a single pull request stay out of the guidance sections: a
request under review describes that request, not how the repository works. Only
the review guide, built from recurring review findings, learns from them.

The guide is a method, not a list. Each pass states a general invariant a future
change must satisfy, keeps the concrete case as an example under it, and ends
with an exit check followed by its obligations, `when <surface> changes → what
must also change`, so a reviewer who sees only a diff can apply the rule.
`PR_REVIEW_GUIDE.md` is the short checklist and `PR_REVIEW_DETAILED_GUIDE.md`
the full method.

The review guides need at least three review findings, drawn from PR discussions
and merged-PR feedback. A repository with fewer keeps only `SKILL.md` and
`CODEBASE.md`. When that happens `init` says why on one line:

    [write] PR_REVIEW_GUIDE.md skipped: found 1 review signals, needs at least 3

The count is what `init` saw, so adding PR sources or another review signal and
running [`sync`](sync.md) can push a repository over the threshold. The
threshold itself does not change.

Evidence and AI job results go into `cache.db` for faster [`sync`](sync.md). A
provider call is retried three times, and if it still fails that one unit is
dropped, or a response that never matches its shape is left out. A format or
provider failure never fails the whole run: `SKILL.md` and `CODEBASE.md` are
still written, and a guide the last run wrote is kept. Fetching and extraction
are cached, so rerunning [`sync`](sync.md) continues without re-fetching. After
`init` succeeds, run [`review`](review.md) on a PR or local changes.

## Agent instruction files

Many repositories keep rules for coding agents in files such as `AGENTS.md`.
Those files are written for an agent that writes code, not for a reviewer, and
they are long. `init` and [`sync`](sync.md) read them and write one short file,
`INSTRUCTIONS.md`, that every review reads with the other guides. A `sync` of a
repository with no matching file sees no change: no new file, no new log line, no
new `--json` field and no extra call. `init` prints one `skipped` line that says
why, see [What the run prints](#what-the-run-prints).

```sh
co-maintainer init owner/repo --max-pr-months=12 --agent-instructions='(^|/)(AGENTS|CLAUDE)\.md$'
```

- **Which files.** `--agent-instructions=REGEX` is a JavaScript regular
  expression matched against the full path of every file on the default branch.
  The default `(^|/)AGENTS\.md$` matches every `AGENTS.md` at any depth. A blank
  value, `--agent-instructions=`, turns the file off and removes an existing one.
- **How much.** `--agent-instructions-max-chars=N` caps the whole file in
  characters. The default is 6000, and `0` or below means no limit. Rules are
  kept in the model's order until the next one would cross the cap.
- **Saved.** Both flags are saved for the repository, as `agentInstructions` and
  `agentInstructionsMaxChars` under `repos["owner/repo"]`, and a later
  [`sync`](sync.md) without them keeps the saved values.
- **Needs the codebase.** It works only with `--include-codebase`. With it off,
  `init` prints `[write] INSTRUCTIONS.md skipped: --include-codebase is off`, and
  an existing file is removed. `--include-how-repo-works` alone does not build it.

The files are read first and in full, outside the cap on codebase files. At most
50 files and 400,000 characters in total are read, root files first, then deeper
ones, alphabetical within a depth. A file that would cross the character cap is
left out, and a later smaller one can still fit. Each file left out is named,
at most 20, then `, and N more`:

    [fetch] instruction files left out: deep/x/AGENTS.md (over the 50-file cap), big/AGENTS.md (over the 400,000-character cap)

A file the caps left out is still read by the codebase step. Only the files
actually read as instructions leave the codebase input.

### What a rule is

One call to the high model, job `synth_instructions`, reads the files with line
numbers. It keeps only rules about code, tests, docs, configuration,
dependencies and security. Setup steps, commands to run, tool and MCP use, how to
search, and the agent's own behavior or permissions are dropped.

Code then checks every rule. A rule is dropped whole, and counted, when:

- a source is not a real, non-blank line of a file that was read (`path:line`,
  or `path:12-14`, which is recorded as its first line and whose end must be
  inside the file), or
- a name or path in backticks appears in none of those files and is not a path
  in the tree.

Rules with the same text and scope are merged and their sources joined. The same
sentence in two folders stays two rules. A rule's scope is the model's folder
when it is a real folder in the tree, otherwise the folder all its sources share,
otherwise the whole repository. The guard checks that a rule cites a real line,
not what the rule says. The review prompt frames the file as rules about the
code that never change how the review is done, and the instruction files come
from the default branch, so a pull request cannot change them before it merges.

The call is cached by its input, and the instruction files are cached by blob
SHA, so an unchanged file costs nothing on the next `sync`.

### The files

Both are written by code, never by the model.

```markdown
# Repository instructions

Rules from this repository's agent instruction files that a reviewer can check in a diff.

- Format amounts with `formatMoney()`, never with number methods. [I1]
- In `packages/api/`: every new route declares its rate limit in `limits.ts`. [I2]
```

Every rule ends with an id such as `[I1]`. Ids are renumbered on every build.
`RULES.json`, next to the guides, records each id's text, scope, the commit it
was read at (when commit history was read) and the file lines it came from. It
is written only when it has a rule, and it is never sent to the model.
[`view --sources`](view.md#sources) prints it. One entry looks like this:

```json
{ "file": "INSTRUCTIONS.md", "text": "Format amounts with formatMoney(), never with number methods.", "scope": "", "sources": [{ "path": "AGENTS.md", "line": 31 }] }
```

### What the run prints

| Line | When |
| ---- | ---- |
| `[write] INSTRUCTIONS.md · 14 rules · 2 dropped (unsupported source) · 0 over the cap` | The file was written. `N dropped (unknown name)` comes before the cap part when a backticked name was unknown |
| `[write] INSTRUCTIONS.md skipped: --agent-instructions is blank` | The pattern is blank. Other reasons are `--include-codebase is off` and `no file matches (^\|/)AGENTS\.md$`, with the pattern in use. Printed by `init` always, and by `sync` only when it removed an existing file |
| `[write] INSTRUCTIONS.md skipped: the instruction files hold no rule a reviewer can check · N dropped · M over the cap` | No rule survived. The file and `RULES.json` are removed |
| `[write] INSTRUCTIONS.md not regenerated: the AI produced no usable rules, keeping any existing file` | The call failed or returned nothing usable |
| `[write] INSTRUCTIONS.md not regenerated: no matched instruction file could be read, keeping any existing file` | Files matched but every fetch failed |

When only some of the files fail to read, the rules are built from the ones that
were read, so a rule from a failed file drops out of that run.

### Flag errors

All are usage errors with exit code 2.

- `--agent-instructions is not a valid regular expression: <the parse error>`
- `--agent-instructions-max-chars must be an integer`
- A saved pattern edited by hand that does not compile: `The saved agentInstructions pattern is not a valid regular expression: <error>` with the hint `Pass --agent-instructions=REGEX to sync to replace it.`

## What it reports

The last line on stderr is the run's cost and time:

    Done in 21.0s · 3,125 in, 1,308 out tokens · $0.0016

When the provider does not report a price the dollar field is `cost unknown`,
and a cache-hit [`sync`](sync.md) that made no AI call still prints the line
with `0 in, 0 out tokens`. stdout is unchanged, so piped output stays clean.
[`review`](review.md) prints the same line.

## JSON output

With `--json`, stdout is a single JSON object (`schemaVersion` `1`) and every
progress line goes to stderr. Fields: `command` (`init` or `sync`), `repo`,
`skillPath`, `changed[]` (the sections this run rewrote, empty when the guide
was already current), `facts`, `pullRequests`, `commits`, `reviewGuide`
(`detailed`, `single`, `kept`, or `skipped`), `validation` (`errors[]` and
`warnings[]`), `usage` (`tokensIn`, `tokensOut`, `costUsd`, `costNote`), and
`durationMs`. `costUsd` is `null` when the provider did not report a price.

`reviewGuide` says what happened to the review guides in this run:

| Value | Meaning |
| ----- | ------- |
| `detailed` | This run wrote `PR_REVIEW_GUIDE.md` and `PR_REVIEW_DETAILED_GUIDE.md` |
| `single` | This run wrote `PR_REVIEW_GUIDE.md` only |
| `kept` | This run had 3 or more review signals but got no usable guide from the AI. The guide files the last run wrote are kept, and `SKILL.md` still links them |
| `skipped` | No guide was written and none is kept. With fewer than 3 review signals, the guide files are removed |

Two more fields appear only when the instruction files did something, see
[Agent instruction files](#agent-instruction-files). `instructions` is
`{ "status": "written" | "kept" | "empty" | "skipped", "rules": N }`, with
`reason` and `counts` (`unsupportedSource`, `unknownName`, `overCap`) when there
is something to say. `ruleChanges` is described on [`sync`](sync.md#json-output).

Without a terminal or saved config, `--json` exits with code 2 instead of
prompting. Errors with `--json` are JSON on stdout as well.

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/sync.md

# `sync`

Refresh repository knowledge after the default branch or pull requests move on.
`sync` re-fetches GitHub data, reuses unchanged evidence from
[cache](caching.md), and regenerates `SKILL.md` and review guides. It costs
less time and API usage than a full [`init`](init.md) when little changed.

> Earlier releases called this command `remake`. That spelling still runs the
> same job, but it is no longer shown in help.

## Before you run

| Check | Why |
| ----- | --- |
| A successful [`init`](init.md) or `sync` for this `owner/repo` | Without cached state, `sync` refuses to start |
| [GitHub auth](authentication.md) | Reads the repo through `gh` or a PAT |
| [AI provider](providers.md) | Token via `set`, `--token=`, or `--env=PATH`, and both models |
| A reason to refresh | New merges on `main`, outdated guides, or review quality drift |

If the repo was never initialized, run [`init`](init.md) (or [`probe`](probe.md)
first for limits). To change `--include-*` or limits permanently, pass flags on
`sync` or run [`init`](init.md) again with the new options.

## Usage

```sh
co-maintainer set --auth=gh --ai=openrouter --token=YOUR_KEY \
  --low-model=openai/gpt-oss-120b --high-model=openai/gpt-5.6-luna

co-maintainer sync owner/repo
co-maintainer sync owner/repo --env=./.env --log-time
```

After the first [`init`](init.md), a plain `co-maintainer sync owner/repo` is
enough: auth, models, limits, and `include-*` choices are read from
[per-repo config](configuration.md#per-repo-memory). You only need to supply the
API token again if it is not in config or env.

On the [dashboard](dashboard.md), **Sync now** runs the same job as this command.

## Parameters

| Flag | Meaning |
| ------ | ----- |
| `owner/repo` | Repository to refresh (required) |
| `--auth=gh` | GitHub CLI (default, or from `set` / config) |
| `--auth=pat` | Personal access token (see [Authentication](authentication.md)) |
| `--github-pat=...` | PAT when not in env or config |
| `--env=PATH` | Load env vars from a file |
| `--ai=openrouter` | AI provider (`openrouter`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `opencode-zen` or `opencode-go`). Required, see [AI providers](providers.md) |
| `--token=...` | Provider API key |
| `--low-model=...` | Model for extraction steps |
| `--high-model=...` | Model for synthesis steps |
| `--include-codebase` | Include default-branch tree and files |
| `--include-pull-requests` | Include PR metadata and discussions |
| `--include-pull-request-changes` | Include PR diffs |
| `--include-commit-history` | Include commit messages on the default branch |
| `--include-how-repo-works` | Include issues / workflow signals when available |
| `--agent-instructions=REGEX` | Files to read as agent instruction files for `INSTRUCTIONS.md`. A blank value turns it off. Left out, the last run's value is kept, see [Agent instruction files](init.md#agent-instruction-files) |
| `--agent-instructions-max-chars=N` | Cap on `INSTRUCTIONS.md` in characters, `0` or below for no limit. Left out, the last run's value is kept |
| `--max-pr-months=N` | Limit how far back PR history goes |
| `--max-commits=N` | Limit commits scanned on the default branch |
| `--max-pull-request-change-lines=N` | Skip oversized PR diffs |
| `--max-comment=N` | Cap discussion comments kept per pull request |
| `--only-request-changed-pr` | Keep only pull requests with at least one `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review |
| `--pr-state=open,closed,merged` | Keep a comma-separated subset of `open`, `closed`, and `merged` |
| `--gh-concurrent=N` | Parallel GitHub fetches (default `1`) |
| `--ai-concurrent=N` | Parallel AI jobs (default `3`) |
| `--json` | One JSON document on stdout, no prompts. Same fields as [`init --json`](init.md#json-output), with `command` `sync` |
| `--debug` | Verbose logs on stderr |
| `--log-time` | Print timing per phase |

**Defaults on `sync`:** With no flags, auth, models, `include-*`, `max-*`,
`--only-request-changed-pr`, and `--pr-state` usually come from
[per-repo config](configuration.md#per-repo-memory) written by the last `init`
or `sync`. Omitted `--max-*` values are also filled from the cached run
state for that repo.

**Include flags:** If you pass **any** `--include-*` on the command line, only
the flags you list are enabled. With no `--include-*` flags, the saved per-repo
choices apply.

**Pull request filters:** `--only-request-changed-pr` applies inside the
`--max-pr-months` window. A dismissed review does not count. Dropped pull
requests skip comment and diff downloads. The run logs
`only request-changed pr · kept N · dropped N`. Off until a run saves it.
`--pr-state` takes `open`, `closed`, and `merged`, separated by commas.
`closed` means closed and not merged. With no flag and no saved set, every
state is kept. The listing cache is stored per state set, so a different set
is not filled from the previous listing. `--only-request-changed-pr` does not
turn itself off. To collect every state again, pass
`--pr-state=open,closed,merged`.

## What `sync` says about instruction rules

When the repository has agent instruction files, `sync` rebuilds
[`INSTRUCTIONS.md`](init.md#agent-instruction-files) the way `init` does, and
after the second build it says what changed. The line appears when an earlier
`RULES.json` exists:

    [instructions] 1 rule added (AGENTS.md:40) · 1 rewritten (I3, AGENTS.md:12 joined) · 1 dropped (AGENTS.md:9)

or `[instructions] no rule changed`. Rules are matched by the instruction file
lines they cite, not by their text:

| Change | Meaning |
| ------ | ------- |
| Added | The rule shares no source with any old rule |
| Rewritten | The rule shares a source with an old rule, and its sources or its text changed |
| Dropped | None of the old rule's sources is in any new rule |

The line lists at most 5 sources for added or dropped rules and at most 3
rewritten rules, then `, and N more`. Because a rule is matched by `path:line`, a line inserted at
the top of `AGENTS.md` shifts every line number, so every rule shows as dropped
and added.

A plain `sync` of a repository with no instruction file changes nothing about its
output.

## JSON output

`sync --json` prints the same document as [`init --json`](init.md#json-output),
with `command` `sync`. When the instruction files did something it also has
`ruleChanges`. It is `null` without an earlier `RULES.json`, otherwise it lists
the same three kinds of change in full. `previous` holds the ids of the old
rules a rewritten rule came from, `joined` the sources it gained and `left` the
sources it lost:

```json
{
  "instructions": {
    "added": [{ "id": "I4", "text": "...", "sources": ["AGENTS.md:40"] }],
    "rewritten": [{ "id": "I3", "text": "...", "previous": ["I2"], "joined": ["AGENTS.md:12"], "left": [] }],
    "dropped": [{ "id": "I2", "text": "...", "sources": ["AGENTS.md:9"] }],
    "unchanged": 11
  }
}
```

## What gets reused

- Unchanged files on the default branch (tree SHA in cache)
- Pull request listings and discussions when `updated_at` is unchanged
- Diffs when the PR head SHA is unchanged
- AI extraction and synthesis jobs when inputs and models match

Changed evidence invalidates only the facts and skill sections that depend on
it. Outputs still land under `<config dir>/repos/owner/repo/` (see
[Caching](caching.md)).

`CODEBASE.md` is rebuilt section by section, and a section keeps what it had
unless this run has a reason to change it:

- A section whose facts did not change keeps its text. A rebuilt section takes
  the new text, and one the model had nothing durable to say about is dropped.
- A section whose AI call failed after its retries keeps its old text.
- A section that has facts but is missing from the file is rebuilt, which also
  repairs a `CODEBASE.md` that an earlier version cut short.
- After a full rebuild, for a new high model or a new synthesis version, no old
  text is kept.

When the guide call fails, `sync` keeps the review guides the last run wrote,
`SKILL.md` keeps its link to them, and `--json` says `reviewGuide` `kept`, see
[`init --json`](init.md#json-output).

## Scheduled sync

A [`serve`](serve.md) instance can run `sync` for you. Open a repository in the
dashboard, go to **Settings**, and fill **Scheduled sync** with a five field
cron expression (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week). Leave it blank
to turn it off.

| Example | Runs |
| ------- | ---- |
| `0 3 * * 1` | Every Monday at 03:00 UTC |
| `30 4 * * *` | Every day at 04:30 UTC |
| `0 */6 * * *` | Every six hours, on the hour |

- Times are UTC.
- The minute field takes a single value, so a schedule fires at most once an
  hour. A sync spends model tokens, and this keeps a typo from burning them.
- As in classic cron, a day field that starts with `*` counts as unrestricted, so
  both day fields must match. `0 0 */2 * 1` runs only on Mondays that fall on an
  odd day of the month. When neither day field has a `*`, either one matching is
  enough.
- A repository is skipped while its first setup is unfinished or while another
  setup or sync for it is queued or running.
- A minute the server was down for is not made up. The next matching minute runs.
- The scheduler lives inside `serve`, so nothing runs while `serve` is stopped.

The schedule is stored per repository as `remakeCron` in
[`config.json`](configuration.md#per-repo-memory). The key keeps its original
name so existing config files keep working.

Next: [`review`](review.md). For a one-off refresh before a local review, see
`--sync-before-review` in [local review](local-review.md).

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/view.md

# `view`

Print the guides co-maintainer generated for a repository. This is the way to
see exactly what a review will be judged against, without starting a review.

The guides are the output of [`init`](init.md) / [`sync`](sync.md):
`SKILL.md`, `CODEBASE.md`, the review guides, and `INSTRUCTIONS.md` when the
repository has agent instruction files. They live under the config
directory, not in your clone. See [Caching: Generated guides](caching.md#generated-guides).

## Usage

```sh
co-maintainer view                                  # every guide for the detected repo
co-maintainer view owner/repo                       # every guide, with headers
co-maintainer view owner/repo review-guide          # one guide, raw
co-maintainer view owner/repo instructions          # INSTRUCTIONS.md, raw
co-maintainer view owner/repo --list                # file, size, build date
co-maintainer view owner/repo --path                # the directory they live in
co-maintainer view owner/repo --sources             # each instruction rule and its source lines
co-maintainer view owner/repo --remote              # read from the review server
```

With no repository argument, the name is detected from the `git` remote in the
current directory.

## What it prints

With no guide named, every guide is printed in reading order, each under an
`== SKILL.md · built 2026-09-22 ==` style header. Naming one guide prints that
file raw, with no header, so the output can be redirected straight to a file:

```sh
co-maintainer view owner/repo review-guide > PR_REVIEW_GUIDE.md
```

A guide name is matched case-insensitively as either the page name
(`review-guide`) or the file or body name. `--list` lists every file in the
folder, including any file co-maintainer did not write, with its size and date.

## Sources

[`INSTRUCTIONS.md`](init.md#agent-instruction-files) is built from the repository's
agent instruction files, and each rule in it ends with an id such as `[I1]`.
`--sources` lists every rule by id with the file lines it came from:

```
$ co-maintainer view owner/repo --sources
INSTRUCTIONS.md
  I1  Format amounts with formatMoney(), never with number methods
      AGENTS.md:31 · packages/billing/AGENTS.md:8
```

`--sources --json` prints `RULES.json` as it is. `RULES.json` is the data behind
this view. It is never printed by plain `view`, by `--list` or by a single-guide
view. `--sources` works with `--remote`, which reads the copy the server holds.

These are usage errors with exit code 2:

| Message | When |
| ------- | ---- |
| `--json needs --sources.` | `--json` without `--sources` |
| `--sources cannot be combined with --list or --path.` | Both given |
| `<owner/repo> has no RULES.json.` | No rule was built. The hint is `co-maintainer sync <owner/repo>` |
| `RULES.json for <owner/repo> could not be read.` | The file is not valid. The hint is the same |

## Reading from the server

`--remote` reads the copies a configured [`serve`](serve.md) instance holds,
using the same remote token as [`review --remote`](remote-review.md). The output
format is identical, only the source differs. This is how you check what the
team's shared context says without downloading anything.

`--path` is local-only and is refused with `--remote`, because the directory
belongs to the machine you are on. A rejected token prints the same Settings
hint that `review --remote` prints.

## Before you run

| Check | Why |
| ----- | --- |
| A successful [`init`](init.md) or [`sync`](sync.md) for the repo | Without guides there is nothing to print |
| For `--remote`: a host and token | See [Remote review](remote-review.md) |

If no guides exist, `view` exits with code `2` and suggests
`co-maintainer probe owner/repo`.

## Related

- [`init`](init.md) and [`sync`](sync.md) build and refresh the guides.
- [Caching](caching.md) shows where they are stored.
- [Configuration](configuration.md) lists the flags for each command.

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/review.md

# Review

AI code review using guides from [`init`](init.md) / [`sync`](sync.md).
Progress and diagnostics go to **stderr**. The result goes to **stdout** (human
text or JSON with `--json`).

This page helps you **pick a mode**. Commands, flags, and checklists live on the
linked pages below.

## Which mode should I use?

Start with what you are trying to review, not the flag name.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  start([What are you reviewing?])
  start --> q1{GitHub pull request<br/>by number?}
  q1 -->|yes| pr[PR review]
  q1 -->|no| q2{Uncommitted or local<br/>commits in a clone?}
  q2 -->|not yet| clone[Clone the repo and make your changes]
  q2 -->|yes| q3{Use shared guides<br/>on serve?}
  q3 -->|no, init locally| local[Local review]
  q3 -->|yes, team context| remote[Remote review]

```

| If this sounds like you | Mode | Read next |
| ----------------------- | ---- | --------- |
| You are in a clone and want feedback on your branch or working tree before you open a PR | [Local review](local-review.md) | Your AI provider on your machine, guides on disk |
| Same as local review, but the repo is already inited on [`serve`](serve.md) and you skip per-laptop init/sync | [Remote review](remote-review.md) | Shared context on the server, diff from your clone |
| You have a PR number and do not need to check out that branch locally | [PR review](local-pr-review.md) | `gh` only, guides on disk, AI on your machine |
| You push straight to `main` with no pull request | [Commit watch](commit-watch-review.md) | The server reviews each push, from the GitHub App or CI (`review --remote --range`) |

PR review and remote review **do not combine**: `--remote` is only for a local
diff with no PR positional arguments.

## How the three modes differ

Same underlying guides from `init` / `sync`, different **subject** (what gets
reviewed) and **who keeps that context up to date**.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph context["Guide context"]
    disk["Per laptop: init / sync"]
    shared["Per repo on serve: init / sync once"]
  end

  subgraph subject["What gets reviewed"]
    direction LR
    diff["Git diff in your clone"]
    pr["PR metadata and patch via gh"]
  end

  diff --> localN["Local review"]
  diff --> remoteN["Remote review"]
  pr --> prN["PR review"]

  disk --> localN
  disk --> prN
  shared --> remoteN
```

| | Local review | PR review | Remote review |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Typical moment | Pre-push in your clone, you own local guides | Open PR by number, you own local guides | Pre-push using the team's shared server context |
| Who runs init/sync | You on the laptop | You on the laptop | Ops on the server (you usually do not) |
| Guides at review time | Laptop cache | Laptop cache | Server dashboard repo |
| Extra setup | [AI provider](providers.md) | `gh auth login` and an [AI provider](providers.md) | `serve`, token, `set --remote-host` |
| Deep dive | [local-review](local-review.md) | [local-pr-review](local-pr-review.md) | [remote-review](remote-review.md) |

Team-wide **automatic** PR reviews on webhooks are not a fourth `review` mode.
They go through [`serve`](serve.md) and the GitHub App, and a
[review policy](review-policy.md) decides which pull requests they review. Use PR
review when **you** run the CLI against one PR. To run a remote review on every
pull request from a workflow, use the [GitHub Action](ci.md).

## Depth: `--improve-matrix`

Reviews share one depth control, `--improve-matrix=N`. `1` is the default. Each
step up adds another pass that audits the draft against the complete diff and the
guides, and raises the output budget so a longer answer fits. The pass preserves
valid findings, corrects inaccurate ones, removes duplicates, and adds what the
first pass missed. More passes cost more tokens and take longer. `2` is a
reasonable step up when a change is high risk or the repository is large. The
value is capped at `4`. See [Cost](cost.md) for what a pass costs.

## Large diffs

A review never cuts a diff without saying so. Each changed file ends in one of
five states, and every output reports them.

| State | What the model received |
| ----- | ----------------------- |
| `full` | The whole patch |
| `partial` | The first 12,000 characters of the patch, cut at a line end |
| `summarized` | A low-model summary of the patch |
| `dropped` | Only the path and the line counts, under `NOT SHOWN (diff budget)` in the prompt. The file is not reviewed this round |
| `withheld` | Nothing, because GitHub sent no patch for it |

A diff that fits is sent exactly as it was before this existed. The limits are
constants, not settings:

- A patch over 12,000 characters is `partial`.
- The whole DIFF section, its lists included, never passes 240,000 characters.
- Only a patch over 4,000 characters is summarized, and at most 40 files per
  review. A file over 500 changed lines is summarized when its patch is over
  4,000 characters.
- A list in the prompt names at most 200 files, then `- and N more`.

### How a diff is planned

The preference is always `full`, then `partial` or `summarized`, then `dropped`.

1. A file over 500 changed lines, with a patch over 4,000 characters, is
   summarized, the 40 largest first.
2. A patch over 12,000 characters is `partial`.
3. Over budget, every file with no patch text moves into one `NO DIFF TEXT` list.
   Their states do not change, and they never push a file with a patch out.
4. Still over budget and under 40 summaries, the largest `full` or `partial`
   file with a patch over 4,000 characters is summarized.
5. Still over budget, files with a patch are dropped from the end of path order,
   in plain code point order, so a plan is the same on every machine.
6. Room left goes back to dropped files that fit, smallest first. This runs again
   after the real summaries come back.

Files keep their input order in the prompt. A binary file and a pure rename
have no patch text, so each shows one line instead:

- `[<status>: binary file]`
- `[renamed without changes from <old path>]`

Both are `full`, and so is a pure rename on GitHub. The exception is PR review
and push review, where GitHub sends no patch for a binary file and does not say
why, so a binary file there is `withheld`.

### Reading the rest of a file

The model has a `read-full-diff` tool for `partial`, `summarized` and `dropped`
files. It takes `path` (required), `offset` (a diff line, from 0) and `limit`
(at least 1, default to the end), and lines keep their new-file numbers. A
`full` file answers that it is already in the prompt, and a `withheld` one that
there is no diff text.

One answer stops at `reviewReadDiffMaxChars` characters, 20000 by default, and
ends with `[more: call again with offset=N]`. A single line over the cap ends
with `[line cut at N characters, the rest of this line cannot be read]`. Set the
cap with `set --repo=owner/repo --review-read-diff-max-chars=N`, see
[Configuration](configuration.md#the-read-full-diff-cap). A model with no tool
support cannot call the tool. Its prompt says the dropped files cannot be read
here and must not be reported on.

### Which modes catch up on dropped files

A file counts as seen only when the model received it as `full`, `partial` or
`summarized`. A `dropped` or `withheld` file is never seen, so the next round
sends it again. That works only where a review carries its seen files into the
next one.

| Mode | A dropped file in a later run |
| ---- | ----------------------------- |
| Local review | Covered. Run `review` again |
| PR review | Covered. Run `review` again |
| Remote review | Covered. Run `review --remote` again |
| App review, incremental scope | Covered. The round also sends a file the last round dropped when nobody touched it since |
| Push review (commit watch) | Not covered. Every run sends every file again, so the same files are dropped again |
| App review, whole-pr scope | Not covered, for the same reason |

The warning in each result says which case it is.

### Where the result says it

`--json` has `revision.truncated`, true when any file is not `full`, and
`revision.coverage` in every mode:

```json
"revision": {
  "files": 62, "additions": 4184, "deletions": 335, "truncated": true,
  "coverage": {
    "full": 58, "partial": ["src/store/reads.ts"],
    "summarized": ["src/api/routes.ts", "src/store/schema.ts", "src/store/metrics.ts"],
    "dropped": [], "withheld": []
  }
},
"warnings": []
```

`full` is a count and the others are lists of paths. A file carried over
unchanged from the previous round counts as `full`. In PR review, files that
arrived by a merge are not in `coverage`, so the states can add up to less than
`files`. `warnings` has one entry per case:

| Code | Text |
| ---- | ---- |
| `diff_dropped` | `N files were not reviewed because the diff is too large. Run review again to cover them.` in a mode that covers them later, otherwise `... This review mode does not cover them in a later run.` |
| `diff_withheld` | `N files were not reviewed because GitHub sent no diff for them.` |
| `summary_failed` | `The summary of <path> failed, so the review saw its diff instead, up to the first 12,000 characters.` |

A single file reads `1 file was` and `it`. A failed summary does not fail the
review: that file is `partial`.

- **Terminal.** `Coverage: 58 full · 1 partial · 3 summarized · 0 dropped` comes
  after `Summary:` only when a file is not `full`, with `· N withheld` added when
  there is one. With a dropped or withheld file, "No actionable findings." reads
  "No actionable findings in the files reviewed."
- **GitHub review** (the App). The summary gains `Not reviewed (N)` with one row
  per file, at most 20 and then `- and N more`. The metadata always has a
  `Coverage` line. A file name is shown as a code span with its control
  characters removed, so it cannot add Markdown or a mention. Exit codes and the
  verdict do not change.
- **`--output=github`.** The job summary gets the coverage line and the list.
  Dropped files give one `::warning` that points at the job summary. Withheld
  files give no annotation.
- **Remote review.** The server plans the diff. A newer client with an older
  server prints no coverage line, and an older client with a newer server gets
  the new fields in `--json` and ignores them elsewhere.

## Diagrams

A review can include a diagram when a finding is about a flow, a lifecycle or a
data model. `--diagram-runtime` picks the language. It works in PR review and
local review.

| Value | What the review contains |
| ----- | ------------------------ |
| `mermaid` (default) | Mermaid blocks, as before. GitHub draws them |
| `plantuml` | Standard PlantUML between `@startuml` and `@enduml`, in a fenced block tagged `plantuml`. The source is posted as written. GitHub does not draw PlantUML, so the reader sees the source |
| `plantuml-server` | The same request to the model, then each `plantuml` (or `puml`) block becomes an image link on a PlantUML server |

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- | ------- |
| `--diagram-runtime=mermaid\|plantuml\|plantuml-server` | `mermaid` | The diagram language |
| `--plantuml-server=URL` | `https://www.plantuml.com` | The server for `plantuml-server`. An http or https URL with no user name, password, query string or fragment |
| `--plantuml-output-format=svg\|png` | `svg` | The image format for `plantuml-server` |

```sh
co-maintainer review owner/repo 42 --diagram-runtime=plantuml
co-maintainer review owner/repo 42 --diagram-runtime=plantuml-server --plantuml-output-format=png
```

Every value you pass is checked, even one the chosen runtime ignores. A bad one
is a usage error with exit code 2 and nothing is sent. `--remote` refuses the
three flags, because the server reviews with the settings saved for the
repository. [Configuration](configuration.md#diagram-settings) shows how to save
them, which is also how reviews run by the [GitHub App](github-app.md) and
replies to review comments get them.

### With `plantuml-server`, the diagram source leaves your machine

The image link holds the whole diagram source, encoded. co-maintainer builds the
link and never calls the server. The reader's browser, through GitHub's image
proxy, sends the link to the PlantUML server. A review diagram can carry names of
files, functions and services from private code. With the default server that is
plantuml.com. **For a private repository, run your own PlantUML server and point
`--plantuml-server` at it.**

- The source goes through the same secret redactor as the rest of the review
  text before it is encoded, so a token in it shows as `[redacted]` in the
  decoded link.
- co-maintainer does not remove `!include`, `!includeurl` or `!import` lines
  from a diagram. A server you run should use a security profile that does not
  let a diagram fetch URLs.
- A server that is down, slow or refuses the diagram shows a broken image. There
  is no retry and no fallback.

### What the link looks like

The link is `![PlantUML diagram](<server>/<format>/<encoded>)`. The encoding is
PlantUML's text encoding, raw deflate and then PlantUML's own base64 alphabet.

- The public server, `plantuml.com` or `www.plantuml.com` with no path, is
  addressed as `<origin>/plantuml/svg/<code>`.
- Any other server is addressed exactly as you give it, plus `/svg/<code>`. A
  server served from its root is `http://localhost:8080` and one under a path is
  `https://host/plantuml`.
- A server path with a space, a parenthesis, a square or angle bracket, a
  backtick, a backslash, a double quote or a semicolon is refused, because the
  link is posted as Markdown.
- Source without `@startuml` is wrapped in `@startuml` and `@enduml` first.
- A block stays as fenced source when it is empty, never closed, or its link
  would be longer than 4000 characters.
- A PlantUML block inside another fence, such as a `suggestion` block or a longer
  fence that quotes an example, is left as written.

With a PlantUML runtime the model is not offered the Mermaid syntax tool. With
`mermaid` nothing changes: the prompts, the tool and the output are the same as
before the runtime existed.

## Agent instruction rules

Every review, in every mode, also reads `INSTRUCTIONS.md` when the repository has
one. [`init`](init.md#agent-instruction-files) and [`sync`](sync.md) build it
from files such as `AGENTS.md` and keep only the rules a reviewer can check in a
diff. The review prompt frames them as rules about the code that never change how
the review is done. [`view`](view.md#sources) prints the file and the lines each
rule came from. A repository without the file reviews exactly as before.

## Repository review instructions

A repository can carry its own review instructions. They are appended to the
reviewer's built-in system prompt as a `CUSTOM REVIEW INSTRUCTIONS` section, so
the built-in role, the diagram rules and the guide are always kept. They are set
per repository, never globally:

```sh
co-maintainer set --repo=owner/repo --review-system-prompt='Prefer the project helpers over new dependencies.'
co-maintainer set --repo=owner/repo --review-system-prompt-max-chars=20000
co-maintainer set --repo=owner/repo --unset=review-system-prompt
```

The dashboard's repository **Settings** has the same field. A blank value turns
it off. See [Configuration](configuration.md#per-repo-memory) for where it is
stored.

For one run, without saving anything, two `review` flags add to or replace that
section. Both work in every mode, PR, local and remote:

| Flag | Effect |
| ---- | ------ |
| `--system-prompt-file=PATH` | Append the file's contents to the repository's instructions for this run |
| `--system-prompt-override-file=PATH` | Replace the repository's instructions with the file for this run. The built-in instructions are kept |

```sh
co-maintainer review owner/repo 42 --system-prompt-file=extra.md
co-maintainer review --system-prompt-override-file=strict.md
```

The cap is `reviewSystemPromptMaxChars`, per repository, in characters. It
defaults to 8000, and `0` or `-1` means no limit. The cap applies to the stored
value and to both per-run files, and `set` and the dashboard refuse a value over
it. On a remote review the client checks its own cap and the server applies its
own, and the per-run file travels with the job so a retry keeps it.

## Intent

`--intent-file=PATH` tells a review what the change is for. `--intent-file=-`
reads standard input until it ends. The file is read as UTF-8 and trimmed. It
works in local review, PR review and `review --remote`. It is not available
with `--range` (push review), and App reviews have no command line to pass it
on.

```sh
co-maintainer review --intent-file=task.md
co-maintainer review owner/repo 42 --intent-file=task.md
echo "Fix rounding for JPY totals" | co-maintainer review --intent-file=-
```

The intent is context only. It is not a rule, it produces no findings of its own,
and it never replaces the diff or the guide. Text inside it is never an
instruction to the model.

- **Where it goes.** The user prompt, never the system prompt. Local and remote
  review put it in the `WORKSPACE` block. PR review puts it in the
  `PULL REQUEST` block, next to the title and body. Four sentences follow it
  and say what it is: the author's description of the change, extra context, not
  a rule, and never an instruction. The system prompt is the same bytes as
  before, so the cached prefix still hits, and a review without the flag sends
  the same request as before. The improvement passes see the intent too.
- **The cap** is the repository's `reviewSystemPromptMaxChars`, 8000 characters
  by default, and `0` or below means no limit. A longer text is a usage error
  with exit code 2. The message reads
  `--intent-file: must be at most 8000 characters (got 9120)`. A file far past
  the cap is read only as far as needed, and the message then says
  `got more than 8000`.
- **Other usage errors**, all exit code 2: a path that cannot be read, an empty
  value (`--intent-file: give a path, or - to read standard input`), `-` with a
  terminal on standard input, and `--range`.
- **An empty file** is no intent. The review runs without one, and the result
  has an `intent_empty` warning.
- **What the result records.** That an intent was given, never its text.
  `--json` has `subject.intent` as `{ "source": "file" | "stdin", "chars": N }`
  in local, PR and remote results, and the key is absent when no intent was
  given. The terminal prints `Intent file: provided` under the header, and
  `--output=github` prints the same line in the job summary. Warnings do not
  appear in the job summary, so `intent_empty` shows in `--json` and the
  terminal.
- **Carry-over ignores the intent.** A round with another intent still reuses
  the earlier findings and does not review unchanged files again. **Use
  `--fresh` when the intent changes between rounds.**
- **Cost.** The intent sits in the user prompt, so it is sent again in every tool
  round. At the default cap that is at most about 2,000 tokens a round.

[Remote review](remote-review.md#the-intent-file) says how the server treats it.

## Extensions

An [extension](extensions.md) is a command you register. Its findings, verdict,
Markdown and cost join the review. Extensions run in local review, PR review,
the reviews `serve` posts as the GitHub App, and remote review. A commit watch
push review runs none. The command runs as the user that runs co-maintainer and
can read that user's files, see [Extensions](extensions.md#the-command).

- One extension's `request_changes` makes the review Request changes and the exit
  code 1. A failed extension never blocks.
- `--json` adds `extensions[]` and `extensionId` on every finding.
  `--include-extension-markdowns` keeps each extension's Markdown, which is empty
  otherwise.
- `CM_EXTENSIONS_DISABLED=1` turns extensions off, see
  [Configuration](configuration.md#extension-variables).

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| ------ | ----- |
| 0 | Review finished, no open blocking findings |
| 1 | Review finished, at least one blocking finding, or an extension requested changes |
| 2 | Usage or precondition error (init missing, not a git repo, etc.) |
| 3 | Runtime failure or abort |

### A tree with no changes

A local or remote review of a tree with no changes prints `No changes to review.`
and stops. With `--json` it prints one JSON document instead. It makes no model
call, sends nothing to the server and exits 0.

### Stopping a local review with Ctrl-C

Ctrl-C or SIGTERM stops a local review. The model call in flight is stopped and
no new one is sent, also during a rate-limit wait and at the codegraph install
prompt. The review saves nothing, releases its lock and exits with code 3. With
`--json`, stdout is this one document, and without it nothing more is printed:

```json
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"aborted","message":"Review canceled."},"exitCode":3}
```

A second Ctrl-C ends the process at once. A [`sync`](sync.md) run before the
review with `--sync-before-review` stops at its next AI call. Its GitHub reads
and the codegraph index step are not interrupted, so the review stops after them.

Ctrl-C at any other prompt, in `init`, `sync`, `clear`, `rollback`, `uninstall` or
a review asking for a missing model or key, ends the command as Ctrl-C ends it
anywhere else. It is never read as an answer.

### A repository without guides

A repository that was never initialized has no guides, and no review can run.
Every mode stops the same way, in the terminal, with `--json` and with
`--output=github`: the code is `not_initialized` and the exit code is 2.

```json
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"not_initialized","message":"Review guides are missing for owner/repo.","hint":"co-maintainer init owner/repo"},"exitCode":2}
```

In the terminal the message goes to stderr, then the line
`Hint: co-maintainer init owner/repo`, and stdout stays empty. PR review and
remote review put `[error] ` in front of the message, like every other error of
those modes. Local review and PR review hint `init` on your machine. The guides
of a remote review live on the server, so `init` on your machine would not fix
it, and the message names the server instead:

```
[error] Review guides are missing for owner/repo on review.example.com.
Hint: Run co-maintainer init owner/repo on the server at review.example.com.
```

This holds for `review --remote` and for `review --remote --range`. The one
exception is a push to a repository the [GitHub App](github-app.md) already
covers. The App marks that commit's check run as skipped, so the command prints a
notice saying so and exits 0, see [commit watch](commit-watch-review.md).

A repository the server does not know is a different error, `repo_unavailable`,
see [Remote review](remote-review.md#errors-from-the-server).

### What counts as blocking

`reviewBlocking` in `config.json` decides it, and the same rule is used by
local, PR, remote and the automatic GitHub App reviews.

| Value | A finding blocks when |
| ----- | ----- |
| `model` (default) | The model says so. A P0 always blocks, even if the model labeled it otherwise. |
| `severity` | Its severity is P0 or P1. P2 and P3 never block, whatever the model said. |

The default keeps the 0.4.13 behavior. `severity` exists because the model's
own label can move between two reviews of the same code, which flipped the exit
code for the same finding. With `severity` the same finding set always yields
the same exit code, the same `blocking` count in `--json`, and the same GitHub
review type.

```sh
co-maintainer config set --review-blocking=severity
co-maintainer config set --review-blocking=model      # back to the default
```

`CO_MAINTAINER_REVIEW_BLOCKING` overrides it for one environment.

The automatic GitHub App review picks its type from the open findings only.
With none open, including a re-review whose earlier findings were all fixed, it
approves. With open findings, `model` requests changes, and `severity` requests
changes for a P0 or P1 and comments otherwise.

## JSON output

With `--json`, stdout is a single JSON object (`schemaVersion` `1`). Fields
include `mode` (`local`, `remote`, or `pr`), `subject`, `summary`, `findings[]`,
`warnings[]`, `usage`, and `durationMs`. Every mode includes `revision`, which
counts the files and says which of them the model received in full, see
[Large diffs](#large-diffs). Local and remote runs also include `codegraph`
state. `extensions` is always an array, empty when nothing is registered, and
every finding has `extensionId`, which is `null` for an AI finding, see
[Extensions](#extensions). `subject.intent` is there only when the review was
given an [intent](#intent). Errors with `--json` are JSON on stdout as well.

Flag details per mode: [Local review](local-review.md), [Remote review](remote-review.md),
[PR review](local-pr-review.md).

## GitHub output

`--output=github` prints the findings as GitHub workflow annotations and writes a
table to the job summary, for a run inside GitHub Actions. It works in all three
modes and cannot be combined with `--json`.

- Each finding that is still open becomes one command on stdout, `::error` when it
  blocks and `::warning` when it does not, with its file, line span and a short
  title. A finding closed since the last review is not annotated.
- When `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` is set, a table of every finding, the cost and the
  time is appended to it. An unknown cost reads `cost unknown` with the reason.
- The exit code is the same as without the flag, so a blocking finding fails the
  step.
- Nothing else goes to stdout in this mode. Every finding is one escaped line, so
  text from a pull request can never start a workflow command of its own.

GitHub shows at most ten errors and ten warnings per step. When there are more,
one notice says how many were left out, and the job summary lists all of them.
[CI](ci.md) shows it inside a workflow.

## Human output

Without `--json`, all three modes print the **same** format. Only the header
names the mode, because the subject differs:

```
co-maintainer review · owner/repo · my-branch
4 files · +12 −3 · guide built 2026-09-15 · codegraph used

New (1)
  • src/app.ts:16-18  [P1 · blocking] the gate ignores its threshold
    A violation exactly at the threshold passes.

Still open (1)
  • src/util.ts:4  [P2 · non-blocking] the helper ignores its argument

Closed (1)
  ✓ src/old.ts:9  [P2 · non-blocking] the dead branch

Summary: 1 new · 1 open · 1 closed · 2 blocking
```

Findings are grouped `Closed`, `Still open`, `New`, each labeled with the same
`blocking` decision the exit code uses. The header names the real guide build
date (`guide unknown` only when no guide timestamp can be read) and the state
the run actually reached: `codegraph used`, `codegraph disabled`, or
`codegraph unavailable`: the last one when codegraph was requested but could
not be prepared, which is also what `--json` reports. When a file did not reach
the model in full, a `Coverage:` line follows the summary, see
[Large diffs](#where-the-result-says-it).

The severity legend and the "If you'd like me to explain it in more detail,
please ask." sentence are **not** in terminal output: a terminal has nobody to
ask, and the legend is fixed noise. Both stay in the GitHub review comment,
which is a different reader.

## How findings are produced

The model is asked for a JSON object, not for prose. For each finding it returns
the severity, whether it blocks, the path and line span, the symbol, a title, the
explanation, and an optional replacement. `co-maintainer` renders the Markdown
from that object, so a finding's boundaries are never guessed from the model's
wording. The JSON schema is sent as structured output in the provider's own format
when the provider accepts it. A provider that rejects the combination gets one request
without the schema, and the prompt also asks for a fenced JSON block.

If the answer is not usable JSON, the request is retried once and then, if it
still fails, the older Markdown parser reads it. That parser accepts the em
dash or `:` as the heading separator, so answers written before this change (and
carry-over records saved by `0.4.13`) keep working. The `--json` output and the
human output are both built from the same parsed findings, so they can never
disagree.

## Before any review

| Check | Why |
| ----- | --- |
| [`init`](init.md) or [`sync`](sync.md) on your laptop | Required for local and PR review |
| An [AI provider](providers.md) for local and PR review, with both models saved | AI runs on your machine, and no model is picked for you |
| [Remote setup](remote-review.md) for `--remote` | Host, token, repo already inited on the server |

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/local-review.md

# Local review

Review **staged, unstaged, and untracked** files in your git clone against a
base branch. AI and guides run on **your machine**, with the
[AI provider](providers.md) you saved.

Overview: [`review`](review.md).

## Before you run

| Check | Why |
| ----- | --- |
| Run from the repo root (or a subdirectory with a git root) | Review needs a working tree |
| `origin` or `upstream` points at GitHub (or use `--repo=owner/repo`) | Maps the clone to guides for that repo |
| [`init`](init.md) / [`sync`](sync.md) for that `owner/repo` | `SKILL.md` and review guides on disk |
| A provider key in `set`, `--token=`, or `--env=PATH` | Local review uses your [provider](providers.md) |
| Clean enough git state | Conflicts or broken git state can fail collection |

## Usage

```sh
cd your/clone
co-maintainer review
co-maintainer review --json
co-maintainer review --fresh
co-maintainer review --to-branch=main --sync-before-review
```

## Parameters

| Flag | Meaning |
| ------ | ----- |
| `--json` | One JSON document on stdout, no prompts |
| `--disable-codegraph` | Skip codegraph tools (default is on) |
| `--allow-tool-install` | Install pinned codegraph without a prompt when missing |
| `--fresh` | Ignore carry-over from the previous local review on this branch |
| `--intent-file=PATH` | What the change is for, from a file or `-` for standard input. Context only, read into the `WORKSPACE` block, see [Intent](review.md#intent) |
| `--diagram-runtime`, `--plantuml-server`, `--plantuml-output-format` | The diagram language of the review, see [Diagrams](review.md#diagrams) |
| `--to-branch=<name>` | Base branch for the diff (default: remote default branch) |
| `--branch=<name>` | Branch name when HEAD is detached |
| `--repo=owner/repo` | Override GitHub remote detection |
| `--sync-before-review` | Run [`sync`](sync.md) before reviewing (requires `gh`) |
| `--include-extension-markdowns` | With `--json`, keep each extension's Markdown, which is empty otherwise |
| `--debug` | Verbose logs on stderr |
| `--log-time` | Print timing per phase |

Registered [extensions](extensions.md) run in a local review too, in your working
directory, and their findings join the result.

Do not pass `owner/repo` or a PR number. That selects [PR review](local-pr-review.md)
instead.

## Codegraph

Local review uses codegraph to follow calls between files. On the first run the
pinned build is usually missing, and co-maintainer asks before installing it (see
[Caching](caching.md) for the per-version tools directory). The question names
the package, where it comes from, what it is for, the approximate download size,
and the exact install directory:

```
co-maintainer uses codegraph 1.6.0 (@colbymchenry/codegraph from npm, ~250 MB) to follow calls between files while reviewing.
Install it into <tools dir>/codegraph/1.6.0 (your global PATH is not touched)? [y/N]
```

The question is only asked when **both** stdin and stdout are a terminal and
`CI` is unset. With a closed stdin (`</dev/null`), a piped output, or `CI=1`, it
is skipped and review continues without codegraph, printing one line:

```
[codegraph] codegraph 1.6.0 is not installed, reviewing without it. Pass --allow-tool-install to install it, or --disable-codegraph to skip this notice.
```

Pass `--allow-tool-install` to install without a prompt, or
`--disable-codegraph` to skip the check entirely. Neither CI jobs nor pipelines
can hang on the question. Full details, including the install table and the
version-resolution order, are in [Codegraph](codegraph.md).

## Carry-over

Repeated `co-maintainer review` on the same repo root and branch reuses prior
findings (closed / still open / new) via [cache](caching.md). Use `--fresh` to
start clean. If the cache cannot be read or written, review continues with a
`carry_over_unavailable` warning.

Carry-over never replaces the review. Every run scans the whole diff for new
violations **and** re-checks the previous findings. A finding that is still open
is reported as such rather than suppressing a new one nearby.

A change too large for one review is covered over the next runs. A file the model
did not receive is sent again, so run `review` again and read the `Coverage:`
line, see [Large diffs](review.md#large-diffs).

When a guide is rebuilt (`init` / `sync`) after your last review on this branch,
that review's verdicts were made against rules that no longer exist. The next
review therefore starts fresh on its own (no `--fresh` needed), so a stale
finding cannot hide a violation the new guide would catch.

## Developers

```sh
npm run review-local-e2e
```

Temporary worktree, `CM_FAKE_AI=1`, optional `CM_FAKE_REVIEW_FILE`.

---

Source: https://co-maintainer.com/docs/remote-review.md

# Remote review

Same **local git diff** as [local review](local-review.md), but **review guides
come from the server**. The team runs [`init`](init.md) / [`sync`](sync.md)
once on [`serve`](serve.md). Developers clone, set host and token, and run
`review --remote` without maintaining their own guide cache.

The model runs on the server as part of that path. Codegraph tools (when enabled)
still run on the laptop and return results through the tool bridge.

Overview: [`review`](review.md). Requires [`serve`](serve.md) and the
[dashboard](dashboard.md).

## Before you run

| Check | Why |
| ----- | --- |
| Server running `co-maintainer serve` | Hosts remote review API and shared repo context |
| Repo added on the dashboard with **init** / **sync** | Guides live on the server for everyone |
| **Settings → Remote review** token (`cmr_…`) | Bearer auth for the CLI |
| `co-maintainer set --remote-host=... --remote-token=...` on the laptop | CLI knows where to connect (or pass `--remote-host=` / `--remote-token=` for one run) |
| Git clone with the same diff you would use for local review | Command is still `review --remote` with no PR number |

You do **not** need a local `init` / `sync` for that repo if the server
already has it.

PR review (`owner/repo` + number) **cannot** use `--remote`.

## Usage

```sh
co-maintainer set --remote-host=https://your-server --remote-token=cmr_...
cd your/clone
co-maintainer review --remote
co-maintainer review --remote --json --disable-codegraph
# One-off, without saving host and token to the config:
co-maintainer review --remote --remote-host=https://your-server --remote-token=cmr_...
# Or by environment, which keeps the token off the command line:
CM_REMOTE_HOST=https://your-server CM_REMOTE_TOKEN=cmr_... co-maintainer review --remote
```

To run it on every pull request from a workflow, see [CI](ci.md).

## Parameters

Same as [local review](local-review.md) for diff and output flags:

| Flag | Meaning |
| ------ | ----- |
| `--json` | JSON on stdout |
| `--disable-codegraph` | Skip local codegraph |
| `--allow-tool-install` | Allow codegraph install without a prompt |
| `--fresh` | No carry-over from a prior remote run |
| `--intent-file=PATH` | What the change is for, from a file or `-` for standard input. Context only, see [The intent file](#the-intent-file). Not with `--range` |
| `--to-branch=<name>` | Diff base branch |
| `--branch=<name>` | Branch when HEAD is detached |
| `--repo=owner/repo` | Override remote detection |
| `--remote-host=<url>` | Override the configured host for this run (needs `--remote`) |
| `--remote-token=<token>` | Override the configured token for this run (needs `--remote`) |
| `--remote-byok` | Send your own AI key with this review, see [your own key](#your-own-ai-key) |
| `--no-remote-byok` | Do not send it, even when `remote-byok-default` is on |
| `--include-extension-markdowns` | With `--json`, keep each extension's Markdown, which is empty otherwise |
| `--output=github` | Print GitHub annotations and write the job summary, see [CI](ci.md). Cannot be used with `--json` |
| `--debug` | Verbose stderr |
| `--log-time` | Phase timings |

The codegraph question, and the conditions under which co-maintainer skips it,
are the same as [local review](local-review.md#codegraph).

Not supported with `--remote`: `--sync-before-review` (run
[`sync`](sync.md) on the server instead), and `--diagram-runtime`,
`--plantuml-server` and `--plantuml-output-format`. Each is refused with exit
code 2, because the server reviews with the diagram settings saved for the
repository, see [Configuration](configuration.md#diagram-settings).

## Token scope

A remote token is not tied to one repository: any token can review, and read
the guides of, every active repository on the server. Hand a token only to
people you trust with all of them, and revoke a leaked one from **Settings →
Remote review tokens**.

## Reading the server's guides

The same token that authorizes a review also reads the guides the server holds,
so you can inspect what your review will be judged against without downloading
anything:

```sh
co-maintainer view owner/repo --remote            # every guide, with headers
co-maintainer view owner/repo review-guide --remote   # one guide, raw
co-maintainer view owner/repo --list --remote     # file, size, build date
co-maintainer view owner/repo --sources --remote  # the instruction rules and their source lines
```

The output is the same format as a local `co-maintainer view`, with the same
`--list`, single-guide and header behavior. Only the source differs. `--path`
is local-only and is refused with `--remote`, because the directory belongs to
the machine you are on. A rejected token prints the same Settings hint
`review --remote` prints.

## Your own AI key

By default the server's provider and key pay for a remote review. A server can
also let you bring your own key (BYOK), so the review is billed to you and not to
the server. The server still chooses the provider and the models, only the key is
yours. See [AI providers](providers.md).

### From the command line

```sh
co-maintainer config set remote-byok YOUR_KEY          # save the key once
co-maintainer review --remote --remote-byok            # send it with this review
co-maintainer config set remote-byok-default on        # send it every time
co-maintainer review --remote --no-remote-byok         # but not this time
CM_REMOTE_BYOK=YOUR_KEY co-maintainer review --remote --remote-byok
```

`--remote-byok` only works with `--remote`. The key comes from `CM_REMOTE_BYOK`
first, then from the `remote-byok` config value. With `remote-byok-default on` the
flag is not needed, and `--no-remote-byok` turns it off for one run. Before it
sends anything, the CLI prints `Using your own key with the server's provider:`
followed by the provider's name.

The CLI never falls back to the server's key when you asked for your own. Each of
these stops the run with exit code 2 before the diff is sent:

| Message | Why | What to do |
| ------- | --- | ---------- |
| `No BYOK key is set.` | `--remote-byok` with no key anywhere | `co-maintainer config set remote-byok <key>`, or set `CM_REMOTE_BYOK` |
| `This server (version X) does not support your own key.` | The server predates the feature and would ignore the key, so the CLI refuses to rely on it | Upgrade the server, or run without `--remote-byok` |
| `This server does not accept your own key.` | The server's policy is `off` | Run without `--remote-byok` |
| `This server requires your own key.` | The server's policy is `require` and the run did not send one | `co-maintainer review --remote --remote-byok` |

If the host starts with `http://` and is not `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `::1`,
the CLI warns on stderr that anyone on the network path can read the key, then
carries on. Use `https://`. Both stderr lines are
left out with `--json`.

### On the server

The policy is a server setting, `off`, `allow` or `require`:

| Policy | A review without a key | A review with a key |
| ------ | ---------------------- | ------------------- |
| `off` (the default) | Uses the server's key | Refused with 403: `This server does not accept your own key.` |
| `allow` | Uses the server's key | Uses your key |
| `require` | Refused with 403: `This server requires your own key. Run with --remote-byok.` | Uses your key |

Set it under **Settings**, **Remote review**, **Client key policy (BYOK)**, with
`co-maintainer set --remote-byok-policy=allow`, or with the `CM_REMOTE_BYOK_POLICY`
environment variable. The variable wins over the saved value, so a hosted server
keeps its policy. The handshake tells the CLI which policy is in force and which
provider the server uses. It never includes a key or a model.

### What happens to the key

- It is kept in the server's memory for that one review. It is removed when the
  review finishes, is canceled, or is replaced by a newer submit.
- It is never written to `app.db`, to the cache, to the config, or to a log or a
  job log. A test searches the raw database file and every log for a known key
  after a full review.
- If the server restarts while your review is waiting, the key is gone with it.
  The review ends with `Your key was not kept across a server restart. Submit the
  review again.` and the server's own key is never used instead.
- If the provider refuses the key, the error says so and names your key:
  `The AI provider rejected your own key.` Other provider failures are reported
  as what they are.

### Cost

A review sent with a key is recorded as billed to the key's owner. The dashboard
keeps it out of the server's own spend. A total reads `$1.23 + $0.40 BYOK`, the
server's cost first and what clients paid with their own keys after the plus
sign. See [Cost](cost.md).

## Extensions

A remote review runs the [extensions](extensions.md) registered on `serve`, as
review type `remote`, and the registrations on your own machine do not run. The
extension has no working directory with your checkout, because the checkout is
on your machine. Its findings, verdict and cost come back in the result.

## The intent file

`review --remote --intent-file=PATH` sends the text with the review. What it is
and how the result records it is on [Review](review.md#intent). On a server the
text comes from a client, so it is treated as untrusted.

- **The cap.** The client checks the repository's `reviewSystemPromptMaxChars`
  from its own config (8000 by default) before it sends. The server applies its
  own cap to the trimmed text again. A longer text is refused with 400,
  `revision.description: must be at most N characters (got M)`, and the client
  says `--intent-file was refused by the server:` followed by that. A description
  over 200,000 characters is refused with `revision.description: too long`.
- **A refused submit changes nothing.** The branch's running review and its
  carry-over stay as they were.
- **An older server.** The handshake lists `intent` among its features. A client
  that does not find it does not send the text and adds the warning
  `intent_unsupported`, which says "This server (version X) does not support an
  intent, so the review ran without one." The review runs. An older client with
  a newer server sends nothing, and nothing changes.
- **What the server keeps.** Only the trimmed text, in the job's input row until
  the review ends, the same as the diff. It is never written to a log or a
  result. The client sets `subject.intent` itself, so a server cannot change it.
  The characters U+2028 and U+2029 reach the prompt as a newline escape.
- **Push reviews** (`--range`) take no intent, and the server ignores a
  description sent with one.

## Errors from the server

When the server refuses the handshake, the code tells the cases apart. Each of
these exits with code 2 and writes no job.

| Code | Text | Hint |
| ---- | ---- | ---- |
| `not_initialized` | `Review guides are missing for owner/repo on <host>.` | `Run co-maintainer init owner/repo on the server at <host>.` |
| `repo_unavailable` | `The server at <host> does not have owner/repo available for review.` | `Check the owner/repo name, or add the repository on that server first.` |
| `remote_handshake_failed` | The server's own text, with control characters removed | |

`repo_unavailable` is the same answer for a repository the server does not know
